name: Nikola Jokic
playerOutlook: Jokic has been the top fantasy points scorer for six seasons and counting. He is coming off his second straight season averaging a triple-double, in which he notched a career-best 10.7 APG. The Nuggets offense is built entirely around Jokic, and he is surrounded by finishers at every position, which helps him generate assists and also opens up space for his own scoring. Jokic also remains one of the best rebounders in the league. Barring injury, he projects to lead the league in fantasy points yet again this season.

name: Victor Wembanyama
playerOutlook: Wembanyama made a leap in Year 3 as arguably the most impactful player in the NBA. On the fantasy front, he set new career highs in scoring (25.0 PPG), rebounds (11.5 RPG) and field goal percentage (51.2%). He took a step back in both blocks (3.1 BPG) and 3-pointers (1.9 3PG), but he still led the league in blocks by a large margin and was top-5 among centers in treys. Wembanyama has missed 54 games over the last two seasons, so durability is a concern, but otherwise he projects as potentially the top producer in category leagues.

name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
playerOutlook: Gilgeous-Alexander won his second straight NBA MVP last season and remains one of the most consistent fantasy producers in the league. The Thunder are built perfectly to accentuate his strengths, with finishers and 3-and-D shooters at every position. This provides space for SGA to create off the dribble to generate efficient looks, assist opportunities and free throws galore. He has also averaged almost 72 games per season for the last four campaigns, making him a reliable high-production option.

name: Luka Doncic
playerOutlook: Doncic has won the NBA scoring crown in two of the last three seasons: his last full season with the Mavericks and his first full season with the Lakers. With former teammate LeBron James no longer on the squad, Doncic appears poised for the biggest season of his career. He has massive usage in the Lakers' offense, a talented second option in Austin Reaves to take some defensive pressure off, and finishers at every other position. The main risk is health, with Doncic having missed 50 games over the last two seasons, but when healthy he should challenge for top fantasy scorer in the league.

name: Anthony Edwards
playerOutlook: Edwards set new career bests in scoring (28.8 PPG) and field goal percentage (48.9 FG%) last season and could be set to improve on both marks this season after the Timberwolves traded for point guard LaMelo Ball. Edwards has never played next to an offense creator and facilitator of Ball's caliber, so he should get better looks and easier opportunities this season than he's ever had. Edwards has clear 30+ PPG upside and should again be among the league leaders in 3-pointers made.

name: Donovan Mitchell
playerOutlook: Mitchell has consistently been one of the most productive guards in fantasy, and last season was no exception. The Cavaliers made a big in-season trade, sending out Darius Garland and bringing back James Harden, but Mitchell's numbers remained largely consistent in 22 games next to Harden. Harden is a higher usage point guard than Garland but is also a better distributor which should ultimately lead to better looks for Mitchell. Mitchell's shot volume upside may be slightly capped but his efficiency improvement could be even more impactful.

name: Jayson Tatum
playerOutlook: Tatum missed most of last season but was able to return for the last 16 games. His production was understandably limited, but it was important that he got those games under his belt before resuming his role as the franchise player for the Celtics this season. Tatum will likely assume an even larger role after Jaylen Brown was traded this offseason, and with increased usage he has the chance to turn in his most productive fantasy season if health allows.

name: Tyrese Maxey
playerOutlook: Maxey is coming off a campaign in which he averaged career highs in all six fantasy counting categories: points, assists, rebounds, steals, 3-pointers and blocks. He was fifth in fantasy points per game and fourth in total fantasy points and is still only 25 years old. The 76ers made big moves this offseason, bringing in both Jaylen Brown and LeBron James. While this increases the team's chances to contend, it likely puts a cap on Maxey's volume upside.

name: Jalen Johnson
playerOutlook: Johnson has increased his scoring, rebounding and assists in each of his five seasons up to last season's rounded 23 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists. He stepped forward as the franchise player for the Hawks, particularly after they traded away Trae Young. Johnson moves into this season as one of the few players in the league that has legitimate upside to average a triple-double.

name: Cooper Flagg
playerOutlook: Flagg is coming off a Rookie of the Year campaign but has the potential for major improvements in Year 2. Last season, then-head coach Jason Kidd experimented with Flagg at point guard, an added level of difficulty for a rookie already making the transition to the highest level. This season, new coach Dusty May and returning point guard Kyrie Irving should put Flagg in more advantageous positions to attack defenses. His stats should increase across the board, giving him fantasy upside as high as top-10.

name: Cade Cunningham
playerOutlook: Cunningham set career highs in assists (9.9 APG), steals (1.4 SPG) and blocks (0.8 BPG) last season while turning in the sixth-best fantasy scoring average in the league. Entering his sixth season, Cunningham looks to take another step forward as the team leader for the Pistons and a budding MVP candidate. Cunningham has only played more than 64 games in one season of his career, so durability is of concern, but he has averaged 67 games in his last two seasons ... the best two-season stretch of his career.

name: LaMelo Ball
playerOutlook: After playing his first six seasons with the Hornets, Ball was traded this offseason to the Timberwolves. Ball, the No. 3 overall pick in the 2020 NBA draft will be joining Anthony Edwards, the No. 1 overall pick in the same draft, to form one of the most explosive backcourts in the NBA. Ball is a brilliant, creative offensive talent whose passes and long-range shot attempts often look haphazard even as they prove effective. The biggest question mark is availability; last season was one of only two in Ball's career in which he was able to play more than 51 games.

name: Scottie Barnes
playerOutlook: Barnes has been a metronome of consistency for the past three seasons, averaging a rounded 19 points, 8 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 combined blocks and steals on a year-in, year-out basis. His Raptors made a major move this offseason in bringing back Kawhi Leonard in exchange for Brandon Ingram. Barnes' role should remain similar but his volume and efficiency could actually increase a bit, with similar usage against softer defenses more focused on stopping Leonard.

name: Tyrese Haliburton
playerOutlook: Haliburton is returning after a year away from the NBA recovering from a torn Achilles tendon. In his three full seasons with the Pacers, Haliburton has averaged a rounded 20-10 points-assists double-double with good shooting percentages and almost three 3-pointers a night. While Haliburton may be monitored early in the season, he is more than a year removed from the injury and expected to return to his typical level before long. The Pacers have shooters and finishers at every position, so if he is at full strength Haliburton has the potential to challenge for the league lead in assists.

name: Anthony Davis
playerOutlook: Injuries limited Davis to only 20 games last season and only 29 total with the Mavericks since his midseason trade there in the 2024-25 season. Last season, Davis was traded again to the Wizards though he was never able to play. This season, Davis is expected to return healthy and settle in as the primary big man for the Wizards. He will play next to point guard Trae Young, who excels at running the pick-and-roll and setting up his big man with easy shots. Durability is always a concern for Davis, but if he can remain healthy he could be in for the most efficient scoring season of his career playing next to Young.

name: Amen Thompson
playerOutlook: Thompson was drafted as a once-a-generation athlete with the skill to potentially develop into a lead guard on offense and an elite defensive wing on defense. He has developed rapidly, improving his scoring, rebounding, and assist and steal numbers in each of his first three seasons. Thompson will likely step back as a distributor this season with the return of starting point guard Fred VanVleet, but that should come with a corresponding increase in scoring opportunities with better looks. Still only 23 years old, Thompson should continue to make significant improvements in 2026-27.

name: Bam Adebayo
playerOutlook: Adebayo has been very consistent with his production, and last year was no exception. In the last four years, Adebayo has averaged a rounded 20 points and 10 rebounds while playing about 74 games per year, and last season his averages were within decimal points of his four-year mark in every major category except field goal percentage (down) and 3-pointers (up significantly). Both of those should be helped by the presence of new teammate Giannis Antetokounmpo, who demands defensive help and should open up easier shots for the veteran Adebayo.

name: Derrick White
playerOutlook: White ranked 19th on the ESPN Player Rater last season, an unexpectedly high result. But White contributes positively to every fantasy category, including blocks (1.3 BPG last season), and those net positive contributions add up with no corresponding negatives. White's role remains consistent, and could even be a bit larger with Jaylen Brown traded away over the offseason, making White a great candidate to outperform his likely ADP, particularly in category leagues.

name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
playerOutlook: Antetokounmpo ended his storied career with the Bucks this offseason and will begin a new chapter with the Heat. Antetokounmpo has been one of the most consistent producers in fantasy this generation; in the seven seasons leading up to last, he averaged a rounded 30 points, 11 rebounds and 6 assists per game. Injuries limited him to only 36 games in 2025-26, but if he stays healthy Antetkounmpo should bounce back to his typical production this season.

name: Kawhi Leonard
playerOutlook: Leonard set new career-highs in scoring (27.9 PPG), 3-pointers (2.6 3PG) and free throw percentage (89.2 FT%) last season while playing in his second-most games (68) since 2016-17. In the offseason, he was traded back to the Raptors where he will reprise a similar role. Availability, as always, is the biggest concern with Leonard's fantasy potential: he has only played more than 57 games only twice in his last six seasons.

name: Karl-Anthony Towns
playerOutlook: Towns modified his game last season to fit in with his strong Knicks teammates, turning in his lowest scoring average (20.1 PPG) since his rookie season with his fewest 3-pointers (1.5 3PG) since 2018-19. On the positive side, Towns still has averaged more than 20 PPG in 10 straight seasons and has posted 12.4 RPG in his two seasons with the Knicks, his best marks since 2018-19. Towns also emerged in the playoffs as a strong passer that can generate big assist numbers, should the team decide to run more offense through him.

name: Jamal Murray
playerOutlook: Murray played 75 games last season, his highest numbers since the 2018-19 season. He reached a new peak in his ninth season, establishing career highs of 25.4 PPG, 7.1 APG and 4.4 RPG. Those numbers are similar to Murray's typical playoffs averages, but this was the first time he performed at that level in the regular season. Murray has perfected the art of playing off Nikola Jokic, and as long as his health allows he should be in line for similar or better production in this campaign.

name: Jalen Duren
playerOutlook: Duren took a major leap last season, almost doubling his scoring output from the season before to average a rounded 20-10 points-rebounds double-double. Still only 22 years old with incredible athletic gifts, Duren should continue to improve as he grows into his role as the second star next to Cade Cunningham. Duren gets a high volume of point-blank looks that make him one of the most efficient plus-scorers in the league.

name: Naz Reid
playerOutlook: Reid was the 2024-25 NBA Sixth Man of the Year and has been a metronome of consistent production for the last three seasons with the Timberwolves, averaging a rounded 14 points, 6 rebounds, 2 3-pointers and 2 combined blocks and steals. After being traded this summer, Reid may get starter minutes for the Hornets. If so, he has top-50 upside in category leagues.

name: Pascal Siakam
playerOutlook: Siakam had the second-biggest scoring season of his career in 2025-26 as he tried to pick up the offensive slack with Tyrese Haliburton injured. This might suggest that Haliburton's return could eat into Siakam's numbers, but Siakam has now had more than two seasons to acclimate to the Pacers and establish himself as a franchise cornerstone. With the return of Haliburton's distribution skills putting him in better positions to score, Siakam may retain his elevated scoring this season.

name: James Harden
playerOutlook: Harden was traded to the Cavaliers midseason in exchange for Darius Garland, forming a dynamic backcourt with Donovan Mitchell. Pairing with Mitchell caps Harden's volume. and Harden's usage dropped dramatically after the trade in 26 games last season. In fact, it fell to a value that would have represented the second-lowest season-long Usage percentage over a full season since 2012. Expect his fantasy value this season to be lower than his norm, but even attenuated he remains an impact fantasy starter.

name: Evan Mobley
playerOutlook: Mobley only played 65 games last season due to injury, the third time in his five seasons that he has played less than 70 games. His production largely stayed consistent with the season before, within decimal points of 18 points, 9 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 blocks and 1 steal in both campaigns. At 25 years old, Mobley should still be improving year-over-year, so durability will be the biggest factor in his fantasy potential this season.

name: Kevin Durant
playerOutlook: Durant enters his 20th NBA season as still one of the best scorers in the league. Standing near 7-foot with one of the smoothest jumpers in NBA history, Durant has a playing style that remains effective regardless of age. He is the elder statesman on a talented Rockets team that will get starting point guard Fred VanVleet back this season. Playing with VanVleet should get Durant better looks in the halfcourt offense, so health-willing he could replicate or even surpass his production last season when he ranked 15th in the league in fantasy scoring.

name: Mikal Bridges
playerOutlook: Bridges, the iron man of this generation, has played in every game since he has been in the NBA. That's 638 games and counting. In a league where load management and injuries typically deprives most players of crucial games, Bridges is always available. Though his averages are not eye-popping, he contributes positively across-the-board without any negatives, adding to his value in category leagues.

name: Alperen Sengun
playerOutlook: Sengun is one of the best combinations of post scoring and passing in the NBA; in the last three seasons he has averaged a rounded 20 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists per game with a block and a steal to boot. Sengun has remained a primary scoring option even on a team featuring Kevin Durant, and at only 24 years old he should continue to develop into one of the franchise cornerstones on a talented Rockets roster. Last season, he ranked 14th in the NBA in fantasy points per game.

name: Jalen Brunson
playerOutlook: Brunson reached the pinnacle of the NBA last season by leading the Knicks to their first championship in more than 50 years. He also turned in another strong fantasy campaign, almost exactly in line with his four year averages of a rounded 26 PPG, 3 RPG and 7 APG. The Knicks have one of the more stable lineups in the league, returning the same starting crew with similar roles. Brunson is still squarely in his prime at 30 years old, and his expectations this season should remain right in line with what he has done since arriving in New York.

name: Domantas Sabonis
playerOutlook: Sabonis' season was cut short by a knee injury that limited him to only 19 games, by far the fewest in a campaign in his career. In his three previous full seasons with the Kings, Sabonis had averaged a rounded 19 points, 13 rebounds and 7 assists in 77 games per year. The Kings have signaled a rebuild, letting veterans like DeMar DeRozan walk, and there are rumors that Sabonis could be on the move as well, but as long as he remains in Sacramento expect Sabonis to bounce back to his typical usage levels this season.

name: Nickeil Alexander-Walker
playerOutlook: Alexander-Walker was named the NBA Most Improved Player last season, his first with the Hawks, when he doubled his previous career-high to average 20.8 PPG. Alexander-Walker is a strong shooter-scorer and wing defender that fits in perfectly with the role Atlanta has for him. Playing as a finisher off shots created by Jalen Johnson and working with added space created by the shooting of CJ McCollum, Alexander-Walker should continue to thrive this season.

name: Stephen Curry
playerOutlook: Curry played only 43 games last season, and reportedly there are concerns about the long-term health of his knee going into this season. Entering his 18th season at age 38, durability and availability are legitimate concerns for Curry. He is still an elite producer when he's on the court, but it is risky to draft him early in fantasy leagues.

name: Jalen Williams
playerOutlook: Williams is coming off an injury-riddled season in which he was only able to play 33 games at a career-low 28.4 MPG. After an offseason to get healthy, Williams is expected to bounce back to or even surpass the rounded 22 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists and 2 combined blocks and steals he posted in 2024-25. Still only 25 years old and playing next to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Chet Holmgren, Williams should still be getting better every season.

name: Lauri Markkanen
playerOutlook: Markkanen set new career marks in scoring (26.7 PPG), assists (2.1 APG) and steals (1.0 SPG) last season but also played in a career-low 42 games. Markkanen is the veteran centerpiece for a Jazz team suddenly replete with young talent. Surrounded by Keyonte George and two high-upside wings in Ace Bailey and rookie Darryn Peterson, Markkanen will continue as the primary option for the Jazz but may have more room to operate against defenses that have to focus more on his young teammates.

name: Josh Giddey
playerOutlook: Giddey has increased his scoring, rebounding and assist numbers in both of his seasons with the Bulls. Last season he averaged a rounded 17 points, 9 assists and 8 rebounds and became the clear focal point of the Bulls' offense. The Bulls are in the midst of a rebuild, also featuring rookie No. 4 overall pick Caleb Wilson, but Giddey's usage should be even higher this season and could even come close to averaging a triple-double.

name: Dyson Daniels
playerOutlook: Daniels has been the best thief in the NBA for the past two seasons, averaging 2.5 SPG with the Hawks. This is the centerpiece for his fantasy value, though he does supplement with plus rebound and assist numbers. Daniels has played more than 33 minutes per game the last two seasons, but there is some question if his minutes may shrink since the Hawks brought in three new rotation-level perimeter players this offseason.

name: Devin Booker
playerOutlook: Booker is one of the most consistent players in the NBA. His per-game averages last season were all within decimal points of his averages across the last eight seasons. While his star teammates and supporting cast change, Booker's numbers remain largely the same year-to-year. This should be the case again this season, with games played as the largest variable. In that eight year span, Booker has played as many as 77 games and as few as 53.

name: Kon Knueppel
playerOutlook: Knueppel broke every NBA rookie 3-point record last season and made a serious push to win the Rookie of the Year award ahead of college teammate Cooper Flagg before ultimately ending up as the runner up. Knueppel should have every opportunity to increase his shot share in his second season, though it should be noted that the trade of LaMelo Ball and his floor-general abilities could have a negative impact on the quality of looks Knueppel gets this season.

name: Desmond Bane
playerOutlook: The Magic traded for Bane prior to last season to give them a 3-point threat in a lineup that lacked long-range shooting, and in his first season he averaged more than 20 points with two 3-pointers per game. Bane maxed in both of those categories in 2023-24, when he averaged 23.7 PPG and 3.3 3PG with the Grizzlies. He has the upside to achieve that level of 3-point output this season, particularly if teammates Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner are healthy and siphoning away defensive pressure.

name: Austin Reaves
playerOutlook: Reaves made a star leap last season, proving that he had the capacity to produce major numbers when given the opportunity to. With LeBron James no longer on the Lakers' roster, Reaves now slots as the full-time second option on the team behind Luka Doncic with major upside whenever Doncic is out of the lineup. In four games when both Doncic and James were out of the lineup last season, Reaves averaged a whopping 39.0 PPG and 9.5 APG.

name: Michael Porter Jr.
playerOutlook: Porter thrived in his first season with the Nets, leaning into the lead role to increase his scoring career high by more than five points up to the mid-20s. Porter remains the main option this season even after the trade that brought Julius Randle to town and should continue to produce. The question with Porter is always durability: he has only played more than 62 games twice in his seven-year career.

name: Onyeka Okongwu
playerOutlook: Okongwu's minutes and scoring have increased in each of his six NBA seasons, up to 15.2 PPG in 31.0 MPG last season. Okongwu remains the starting center for the Hawks, making him the second rebounder behind Jalen Johnson and a primary defender notching more than a block and steal per game. He has also worked on his 3-point shot, increasing to 1.9 3PG last season.

name: Donovan Clingan
playerOutlook: Clingan entered the league as one of the best young shot-blockers in the league, then in Year 2 he improved the rest of his game to average a points-rebounds double-double with more than a 3-pointer per game. He has strong upside in points leagues, but it is even higher in category leagues where his shot-blocking and 3-point contributions from the center position are more valuable.

name: Kel'el Ware
playerOutlook: Ware is a prime breakout candidate this season after he was traded to the Bucks as part of the package for Giannis Antetokounmpo. Ware averaged almost a double-double with a 3-pointer, block and steal in about 22 MPG for the Heat last season. His role is expected to be larger in Milwaukee, where he could get near starter minutes in a big man rotation that includes another big with scoring range in Myles Turner. If Ware does get those minutes, he has top-75 upside in points leagues and top-40 in category leagues, where those defensive and 3-point stats are more vital.

name: Trey Murphy III
playerOutlook: Murphy has emerged as a primary option for the Pelicans, a high-volume shooter and scorer that goes on streaks where it seems he can't miss. The Pelicans have developed depth on the wing, with more players than available minutes, but Murphy is a priority that should maintain his role and shots. Murphy does have some durability concerns; in his five NBA seasons, he has only played more than 66 games once.

name: Walker Kessler
playerOutlook: Kessler was limited by shoulder surgery to only five games last season but should be returned to health for this, his first campaign with the Lakers. Kessler has been brought in to be the Lakers' franchise big man: an anchor on defense and a finisher on offense. Kessler is one of the best shot-blockers in the NBA and an athletic finisher around the rim, exactly the prototype for the type of big that thrives next to Luka Doncic. If he stays healthy, Kessler should be poised for the best season of his career with top-50 upside in points leagues and top-30 in categories.

name: Trae Young
playerOutlook: After spending his first seven seasons with the Atlanta Hawks, Young was traded to the Wizards in January. Young battled injury before and after the trade and was limited to only 15 total games played, the fewest in his career. This season, Young will be the leader of a new-look Wizards squad featuring fellow All-Star Anthony Davis and rookie No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa. Young will be surrounded by finishers and potential pick-and-roll partners, which bodes well for a player in Young who increased his assists per game in each of his first seven seasons in the league.

name: Kyrie Irving
playerOutlook: Irving missed all of last season with a torn ACL but is reportedly almost fully recovered. He rejoins a very different Mavericks team, with Cooper Flagg as the new centerpiece and both Luka Doncic and Anthony Davis traded away. Irving is a high-usage guard that adjusted his passing game to play with Doncic; he should have the chance to create more offense and thus better fantasy numbers as the lead guard next to Flagg.

name: Jarrett Allen
playerOutlook: Allen matched a career-low by only playing 56 games last season, but he had averaged 80 games over his previous two seasons and will look to bounce back in this campaign. Allen is a defense/rebound role player that also scores about 15 high-efficiency points per game. His role is well established, and his scoring improved once the Cavaliers traded for James Harden, so the 28-year-old Allen should be expected to produce at a similar or better level again this season.

name: Chet Holmgren
playerOutlook: Holmgren set incremental career highs in points and rebounds last season, but he has the capacity for more improvement in Year 4. The Thunder could use more offense from Holmgren, and if he is more assertive he has the skill and opportunity to become a 20 and 10 player as soon as this season. Add that to his defense and long-range shooting, and Holmgren has top-25 upside in category leagues.

name: De'Aaron Fox
playerOutlook: At 28 years old, Fox finds himself as the grizzled veteran on a team full of young, up-and-coming superstars. Fox's scoring in his first full season with the Spurs (18.6 PPG) was more than six points lower than his average for the five previous seasons (24.7 PPG), in large part because he had to share shots with Victor Wembanyama and Stephon Castle. Also because he had to share minutes with Dylan Harper, who played well as a rookie and seems poised to pop as a sophomore. Fox's minutes and production could go down more this season as the three young stars all take on even larger roles.

name: Darius Garland
playerOutlook: Garland is the franchise player for the Clippers this season after the Kawhi Leonard trade. Garland battled injury last season, but after being traded to the Clippers his numbers went up across the board even playing fewer minutes. Now healthy and in a larger role, Garland appears poised to have the best fantasy season of his career as long as he can stay healthy.

name: Brandon Miller
playerOutlook: Miller's third season was almost a carbon copy of his second on a per-game basis, but he played in more than twice as many games (65) as the season before (27). He, along with sophomore Kon Knueppel, are the two primary scoring options for the Hornets and could get more volume this season after the departure of Lamelo Ball. Ball was the point guard as well, though, so his loss could also mean lower quality shots and those lower scoring efficiency.

name: Rudy Gobert
playerOutlook: Gobert has been a model of consistency on defense and the glass for a decade. For the last two seasons, Gobert had been part of a triumverate of impact big men with Julius Randle and Naz Reid. This offseason, the Timberwolves traded Randle to the Nets and Reid to the Hornets without getting a starting caliber big in either deal. This solidifies Gobert with as many minutes as he can handle, so he seems poised for one of his stronger campaigns.

name: Caleb Wilson
playerOutlook: Wilson is a big forward with explosive athleticism that was in the conversation to be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft before injury shortened his lone collegiate season. Wilson recovered from injury in time to play in the Las Vegas Summer League and unveil a previously unseen 3-point shot. He already projected to produce strong defensive and rebound numbers, as well as scoring in the lane, but the added 3-point range opens Wilson's entire game and makes him a potential fantasy impact player as a rookie.

name: Ty Jerome
playerOutlook: Jerome was limited by injury to only 15 games last season, but what he accomplished in those games was startling. He averaged a rounded 20 points, 6 assists and 3 3-pointers in only 23 minutes per game. Jerome should be in for a larger role for the Grizzlies this season after Ja Morant was traded away. If he can approach his per-minute production with more minutes, he has top-50 fantasy upside.

name: VJ Edgecombe
playerOutlook: Edgecombe turned in an electric rookie season that established him as an impact player in the NBA. But the 76ers brought in several high level wings this offseason, including LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, that could put a ceiling on Edgecombe's upside. He demonstrated the ability to be a 20/5/5 type player with good 3-pointer and defensive numbers, but as the fourth or fifth option on a loaded 76ers team he may instead remain a mid-upper teens scorer with good peripherals.

name: Deni Avdija
playerOutlook: Avdija exploded last season, far surpassing his previous career best marks in scoring (24.2 PPG) and assists (6.7 APG) as he grew into the franchise player for the Trail Blazers. Avdija spent large swathes of the season as a point forward with nightly triple-double upside, but once Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson were healthy Avdija became more of a finisher. He is likely to lean even more into the finisher role this season, with the Trail Blazers fielding at least four starting caliber point guards to fill the floor general slots.

name: Dejounte Murray
playerOutlook: Murray has battled major injuries in each of the last two seasons, limiting him to a total of 45 games played out of a possible 162. He had averaged 76 games the two seasons prior, and if he can return to that level of availability he can again be an impact fantasy starter. His scoring role with the Pelicans is not as large as previous roles with the Hawks and Spurs, but Murray is still a plus contributor to most counting and percentage categories.

name: Reed Sheppard
playerOutlook: Sheppard got major minutes in Year 2, in part due to the injury absence of Fred VanVleet. Sheppard capitalized on those minutes to prove himself a plus shooter-scorer with enough playmaking, rebounding and defense to post positive peripheral numbers. However, VanVleet returns this season and the Rockets brought in Marcus Smart as well. Sheppard still has a key role for the team as a shooter and scorer off the bench, but his fantasy upside may be capped by role and minutes competition.

name: Jaylen Brown
playerOutlook: Brown is coming off his best individual season, operating as the sole focal point of the Celtics' offense with Jayson Tatum sidelined. After being traded to the 76ers this offseason, he is now in the opposite situation with several other high-usage teammates to share the ball with. Brown is in his peak seasons so should play well even with fewer shots, but his shot volume should lower significantly playing next to Tyrese Maxey, LeBron James, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

name: Matas Buzelis
playerOutlook: Buzelis had a major glowup in Year 2, nearly doubling his rookie season stats and establishing himself as a cornerstone for the rebuilding Bulls. He will be the starting small forward in a lineup featuring three new starters in addition to returning point guard Josh Giddey. Buzelis is called upon to provide strong shooting and scoring, as well as to defend and crash the boards. This generates solid across-the-board numbers that gives Buzelis added value in category leagues.

name: Tyler Herro
playerOutlook: Herro was the centerpiece of the package the Bucks received for trading Giannis Antetokounmpo. Herro averaged more than 20 PPG in each of the last five seasons as a contributor on the Heat, but his upside in Milwaukee could be much higher. On a fully rebuilding Bucks team, Herro has the opportunity to maximize his scoring potential. He should get as many shots as he can handle and likely produce the best scoring and assist volume of his career this season.

name: Alex Sarr
playerOutlook: Sarr was the No. 2 overall pick in the 2024 NBA draft, and he has quietly been developing into a starting caliber center worthy of such lofty draft heritage. In roughly the same 27 minutes he averaged as a rookie, Sarr upped almost all of his fantasy stats as a sophomore. He is a strong shot-blocker and defender that appears to have 20-10 point-rebound upside in the near future. His ceiling may be capped this season with the additions Anthony Davis and Deandre Ayton, but if he gets starter minutes Sarr has top-50 fantasy potential, particularly in category leagues.

name: Norman Powell
playerOutlook: Powell broke out two seasons ago with the Clippers, going from a productive scorer off the bench to a 20-plus points starter for first the Clippers and then the Heat. This season he has signed on to be the shooter-scorer wing for the Bulls. He should get plenty of good looks playing off Josh Giddey, particularly if rookie Caleb Wilson is able to play well enough to draw defensive attention of his own.

name: Franz Wagner
playerOutlook: Wagner joined with Paolo Banchero and Desmond Bane to form a big three for the Magic, each scoring more than 20 PPG. But with three big scorers, each has their volume limited. Wagner's scoring average dropped almost four points from the season before. Wagner also has durability questions: he has dealt with injuries in each of the last two seasons, limiting him to 94 out of 164 possible games.

name: Brandin Podziemski
playerOutlook: Podziemski developed into a starting caliber impact player last season, particularly while both Stephen Curry and Jimmy Butler III were out with injury. Curry is back, though both veterans are still dealing with their injuries. Podziemski, then, has a chance to build on his success from last season as the assumed starter at shooting guard. Podziemski has the type of cross-category positive production without any glaring weak areas, making him valuable in category leagues.

name: Damian Lillard
playerOutlook: Lillard sat out last season with a torn Achilles, and when last he played it was as the second option to Giannis Antetokounmpo with the Bucks. This season, he will be back home with the Trail Blazers squad where he spent his first decade in the league. Portland is in the midst of rebuilding and have four strong lead guards, including Lillard, Jrue Holiday, Ja Morant and Scoot Henderson. The minutes distribution isn't clear, though between them they may get minutes at shooting guard as well. Lillard should be productive when on the floor but his volume could be capped.

name: OG Anunoby
playerOutlook: Anunoby is the epitome of a productive 3-and-D wing and he's firmly established in that role for a stable Knicks starting lineup. In addition to his upper-mid teens scoring and handful of rebounds, Anunoby averages more than two 3-pointers and almost 2.5 combined blocks and steals. This gives him higher upside, borderline top-50 in fantasy category leagues.

name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
playerOutlook: Jackson was traded to the Jazz midseason in 2025-26, and only played three games with them before being shut down with a knee injury. He could get more minutes at center with the trade of Walker Kessler to the Lakers, though Jusuf Nurkic is still on roster. But Jackson is young and has the dynamic scoring ability to fit in with the other young Jazz. If he can channel the form that made him the 2022-23 Defensive Player of the Year, Jackson could be a strong blend of shot-blocking and 3-point shooting that makes him more valuable in category leagues than points leagues.

name: LeBron James
playerOutlook: James willingly accepted a third option role with the Lakers last season, allowing Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves to operate at higher usage. After signing with the 76ers this offseason, James finds himself in a similar situation where he will likely be the third or fourth option behind teammates Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid. James may play some point forward, so his assists may increase, but his scoring volume and overall fantasy production are likely capped.

name: Fred VanVleet
playerOutlook: VanVleet missed all of last season with a knee injury, but perhaps more importantly the Rockets missed him. Even with the addition of Kevin Durant last season, the Rockets were only able to win the same 52 games they had won with VanVleet at the helm the season before. VanVleet therefore returns to his role as starting point guard with job security despite the depth of quality perimeter players the Rockets have on roster. His production expectation this season is similar to the 2024-25 campaign, making him a top-100 player that has top-50 upside if he instead returns to his levels from the early 2020s.

name: Ivica Zubac
playerOutlook: Zubac was traded to the Pacers at midseason, but was already dealing with injuries that nagged him for the rest of the campaign. Prior to the injury, while with the Clippers, Zubac was continuing his breakout play from the season before as a dominant rebounder and plus scorer with solid peripheral numbers. Now healthy, Zubac should return to that level while with the Pacers. He will have the added benefit of the return of point guard Tyrese Haliburton, one of the best distributors in the NBA who should get Zubac plenty of great looks.

name: Paolo Banchero
playerOutlook: Banchero struggled with injury in 2024-25 but bounced back to play 72 games last season, the third time in his four seasons he has played at least 72 games. Banchero's game and production have been largely consistent through his first four NBA seasons, but his scoring dipped almost four points per game last season due to increased scoring talent among his teammates. Banchero's volume is slightly capped playing alongside proven scorers Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane.

name: Cameron Boozer
playerOutlook: Boozer was arguably the most professional-ready of the four rookies that were discussed as potential top picks in the 2026 NBA draft. A big forward with a strong inside-out game, the ability to clean the glass and surprising court vision. He is immediately the focal point of the Grizzlies' rebuild effort, and is an early favorite to win NBA Rookie of the Year. He could be a fantasy starter from day 1.

name: Miles Bridges
playerOutlook: After playing the first seven seasons of his career with the Hornets, Bridges was traded this offseason and becomes the new starting forward for the Suns. Bridges' role in Phoenix should be similar to the one he played in Charlotte: a shooter-scorer big forward playing off talented perimeter creators and a supporting rebounder to a defensive role playing center. Though his geography changed, his fantasy value remains similar.

name: Ausar Thompson
playerOutlook: Thompson is the best wing defender on the Pistons, and in that role he generates about two steals and a block per game. He also has points-rebounds double-double upside in any given night, and last season raised his career-best mark to over three assists per game. His weakness is his inability to knock down 3-pointers, and if he were to add the spot-up baseline 3-pointer to his repertoire it would add another dimension to his game and his fantasy value. As it stands, he's a fringe top-100 fantasy option.

name: Kristaps Porzingis
playerOutlook: Porzingis is one of the elite per-minute producers of his generation, but injuries have consistently derailed his availability and is already out for training camp. Porzingis missed 50 games last season and 40 the season before, and has missed at least 16 games in nine straight seasons. He is slotted to be the Warriors' starting center this season, and when he plays he will produce, but he is risky to draft in fantasy leagues before the late-middle rounds at the earliest.

name: Jaden McDaniels
playerOutlook: McDaniels is coming off the best season of his career, and at 25 years old is on the cusp of his athletic prime years. McDaniels' role could be larger this season after the Timberwolves traded away Julius Randle and Naz Reid while bringing in only Jonathan Kuminga as a starting-caliber replacement. He is a jack-of-all trades that scores in the mid-teens, shoots good percentages and contributes 1+ blocks, steals and 3-pointers per game. This gives him major upside in category leagues, with top-50 potential.

name: CJ McCollum
playerOutlook: McCollum was traded to the Hawks at midseason and fit in perfectly with the rest of their lineup in 2025-26. More shooter-scorer lead guard than true point guard, McCollum works with backcourt-mate Nickeil Alexander-Walker to generate points and scoring opportunities for teammates while playing off Jalen Johnson. Fantasy-wise, McCollum's scoring, 3-point shooting, assists and rebounds make him a top-80 fantasy prospect.

name: Keegan Murray
playerOutlook: Murray enters the season as Sacramento’s likely starting power forward after an injury-plagued fourth season. He averaged 14.0 PPG, 5.7 RPG and 1.6 BPG last season, but shot a career-low 27.7% from three. His defensive production gives him fantasy value even when the shot isn’t falling, while a return to his earlier shooting form would raise his ceiling considerably. Murray still has competition for minutes in Sacramento’s frontcourt, but his two-way role should keep him involved. He’s worth a late-round flier in fantasy drafts.

name: Julius Randle
playerOutlook: Randle should be in for a bigger role this season after being traded from the Timberwolves to the Nets. Randle has been the second option to Anthony Edwards for the past two seasons but should have a higher usage on the rebuilding Nets. He, along with Michael Porter Jr., are the only veteran scorers on a team otherwise full of young, developing players.

name: Andrew Wiggins
playerOutlook: Wiggins should open the season as Miami’s third option behind Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. Playing off those two should give Wiggins more catch-and-shoot opportunities and help his efficiency, but it could also keep his usage modest. A breakout season is unlikely, but replicating last season’s production isn’t out of the realm of possibility. Wiggins is a solid target in the double-digit rounds for managers looking for scoring, threes and rebounds.

name: AJ Dybantsa
playerOutlook: Dybantsa was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft and enters the league as a scorer. He led the NCAA in scoring average as a freshman at BYU and was one of the leading scorers at the Las Vegas Summer League as well. Dybantsa has the size of a big forward but the ball-handling ability of a wing. He is great at getting to his spot and scoring from the mid-range, and he is also adept at drawing fouls and getting to the line. Dybantsa has a good chance to lead all rookies in scoring and establish himself as a fantasy starter immediately.

name: Joel Embiid
playerOutlook: Availability is the primary question when it comes to Embiid's fantasy prospects. His production is still elite when he is on the court, but in the last two seasons he has only played in 57 of a possible 164 games. His durability history makes him difficult to draft before the middle-late rounds of fantasy drafts, but if this were the season where he could play even 60 games Embiid could be a league-winning player. The 76ers are chock full of talent with the offseason additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, but when the 32-year-old Embiid is on the court he still defaults to a primary role in the team's offense.

name: Keyonte George
playerOutlook: George broke out last season, settling in as the lead guard for the Jazz and pushing his scoring average up into the mid 20s. He also set new career marks in assists, with the threat of his own scoring imbalancing defenses and helping him create offense for teammates. The Jazz feature Lauri Markkanen as the main scoring option, but George is a close second. His challenge this season will be integrating all-world rookie Darryn Peterson into the backcourt in a way where both are optimized.

name: Derik Queen
playerOutlook: The Pelicans made headlines on NBA draft night in 2025 when they traded an unprotected first round pick for Queen. Queen then went out and turned in an impressive rookie season with rounded averages of 12 PPG, 7 RPG and 4 APG in 25 MPG. While the Pelicans have several talented options in the frontcourt, Queen seems to be a big part of their future plans and thus could push for more minutes and opportunity in Year 2. If he gets starter minutes, Queen has nightly double-double potential.

name: Immanuel Quickley
playerOutlook: Quickley has settled into his role as the lead guard for the Raptors, averaging in the mid-upper teens scoring with close to six assists, four boards and just under three 3-pointers per game. He should benefit from the return of Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors. Defenses will focus more on stopping Leonard, which should give Quickley more space to operate as both a playmaker and a shooter.

name: Paul George
playerOutlook: No outlook available.

name: Stephon Castle
playerOutlook: Castle increased his role and production in Year 2, up from his Rookie of the Year numbers from the season before. He was drafted as an elite defender with the size to guard wings and the speed to guard point guards, but his offense took a big leap as well. He increased his scoring average and almost doubled his assist output. When healthy, the Spurs have two other strong lead guards in De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper that may cap Castle's assist opportunities, but he has room to increase his scoring and has 20 PPG potential in Year 3.

name: Tobias Harris
playerOutlook: Harris enters the season competing with Julian Champagnie for the Spurs starting power forward job. He averaged 13.3 PPG and 5.1 RPG in 63 games for the Pistons last season, then raised his production to 18.1 PPG and 7.2 RPG in the playoffs. Harris brings shooting, rebounding and the ability to create his own shot, but San Antonio’s deep rotation could limit his usage. Winning the starting job would give him a clearer path to fantasy value. Given the circumstances, Harris is worth taking a flier on later in drafts.

name: Zion Williamson
playerOutlook: Williamson played 62 games last season, a positive bounce-back from the 30 he played the season before, and the second-most games he has played in the eight seasons since he was drafted. Williamson also had his smallest role with the Pelicans last season, notching career-lows in both points and rebounds per game. The Pelicans have a lot of startable talent in their frontcourt, including young players they want to build around, so Williamson's role and future with the Pelicans have enough questions to limit his fantasy upside even beyond the availability concerns.

name: Myles Turner
playerOutlook: Turner will be looking to rebound from a disappointing first season in Milwaukee. He averaged 11.9 PPG and 5.3 RPG last season but remained effective from the perimeter, shooting 38.3% from 3-point range. Turner still offers a valuable combination of threes and blocks from the center position, but his declining scoring and rebounding numbers lower the ceiling. Milwaukee’s rebuild also creates some uncertainty around his long-term role. Turner is best viewed as a late round target for managers looking for blocks without sacrificing 3-point production.

name: John Collins
playerOutlook: Collins joined the Pistons this offseason and slots in to be one of their main scoring options in the frontcourt. He has averaged 19 or more points per game three times in his career, including two seasons ago with the Jazz. He excels at playing off an elite point guard, and Cade Cunningham should get him easy looks both at the rim and behind the arc. Collins is a top-100 fantasy prospect, but if he plays to his full capabilities he has top-50 upside in points leagues.

name: Josh Hart
playerOutlook: Hart took a step backwards statistically last season, partially because he was battling nagging injuries for most of the season. He played 11 fewer games with 7.4 fewer MPG than the season before, and that translated to his production. Nevertheless, he remains a dominant rebounder from the wing with plus contributions to assists, 3-pointers and steals who can also average in the low-teens in scoring on 50+ FG%. The Knicks lost some depth this offseason, and if healthy Hart will likely be called upon to return to his more typical 33+ minutes played with the resulting statistical bump this season.

name: Payton Pritchard
playerOutlook: Pritchard's minutes and production have increased in each of the last three seasons, peaking with his rounded 17 PPG, 5 APG, 4 RPG and 3 3PG last season. His role was expanded last season by the injury to Jayson Tatum, and he is likely to maintain that elevated level this season after the offseason trade of Jaylen Brown. Payton is an outstanding 3-point shooter and solid playmaker that the Celtics will rely on again this season, giving him top-50 fantasy upside in category leagues.

name: Dylan Harper
playerOutlook: Harper turned in a promising rookie season, posting solid all-around numbers in 23 minutes per game. He stepped it up in the playoffs, enough so that he is expected to play closer to starter minutes in Year 2. In six starts last season, including the playoffs, Harper averaged a rounded 16 PPG, 5 RPG and 5 APG in 30 MPG.

name: Collin Gillespie
playerOutlook: No outlook available.
